head.name: @fzlt/core/hud
head.lead: Change-only HUD bindings that never allocate in the steady state. A binding reads a number (or a flag) every render, compares it as a number after rounding to what the readout shows, and formats and writes only when that changed. Feeds and banners react to the event ring (engine.events), never to polling. Every write goes through engine.ledger, so destroy() gives the page back. Render phase only: no layout reads, nothing in the step. No visuals of its own: it binds to the game's markup (Board UI or anything else).

sizesNote: Measured on this build: minified and gzipped with everything it imports, the way npm run size checks the budget in CI.

blocks.label: EXAMPLE · typechecked against v0.27.0
blocks.code:
const s = new Float64Array(2); // clock, armor (0..1): fractions in a typed array
hud(e, wrap)
  .num("[data-score]", () => score)        // written only when it changes
  .num("[data-clock]", [s, 0], "clock")    // 2:59
  .meter("[data-hp]", [s, 1], 0.34)        // class "low" at or under 34%
  .feed(".feed", 4, "kill", (a, b) => NAMES[a] + " ✕ " + NAMES[b]);

items.doc: Where a number comes from: a getter, or a slot in a typed array ([state, 3]). A getter V8 doesn't inline boxes a fractional double on every call (16 bytes); a slot never does, so it is the safe choice for running fractions (clock, hp, heat). Whole numbers and booleans never box.
items.code: export type Src = (() => number) | readonly [ArrayLike<number>, number];
